title: Redesign the isComposerEmptied submission oracle around pane geometry instead of content matching
description:
Split out of CAM-358, whose scope was narrowed to the settle-window fix after two review rounds proved this part is a design problem, not a bug fix.

PROBLEM. isComposerEmptied (src/tmux/dispatch.ts) decides whether a pushed [cam] line left the composer by substring-matching the payload against captured pane text. That signal is fundamentally ambiguous and every in-place patch fixed one pane shape while breaking another:

- Joining the tail window also matches the ECHOED submitted line, so a delivered payload reads as still-in-composer and gets resent (reviewer Probe A: ONE logical push produced THREE send-keys calls, plus a spurious push-undelivered event for a push that landed).
- A no-anchor fallback keyed on occurrences >= 2 was calibrated on the integration fixture's `cat` process, which double-echoes (kernel tty live-typing echo + cat echo-back). The production orchestrator pane runs the claude Ink TUI in raw mode, renders the transcript itself, and does NOT double-echo, so a delivered payload appears exactly ONCE and the heuristic inverts in production.
- That fallback counted occurrences over the FULL capture rather than the tail window, so scrollback history changes the verdict. Production wires the full-scrollback reader (host.ts:579-586, capture-pane -p -S -) while unit tests wire the visible-screen reader (dispatch.ts:191-198), so the two disagree on identical pane state.
- Anchoring on the last tail line matching /^\s*[>\u276f]/ is forgeable by the payload itself: a '>' or '->' landing at column 0 of a soft-wrap boundary makes the join start mid-payload, isComposerEmptied returns delivered for a still-composing push, and the line is silently lost with no retry and no event. '->' is realistic in [cam] status text.

DIRECTION (reviewer's recommendation). Anchor on a shape the payload cannot forge: track the composer row index from pane geometry (e.g. tmux cursor position via display-message -p '#{cursor_y}' / '#{cursor_x}', or pane dimensions) rather than regex over pane content. Geometry is unforgeable by payload text and is independent of which capture reader is wired.

CONSTRAINTS LEARNED.
- Any oracle must be correct for BOTH directions: a delivered payload must not be resent (duplicate sends trip the back-to-back send-keys race at scripts/cam/patterns.md:330), and an undelivered payload must not be reported delivered (silent loss, the original CAM-358 bug).
- Test fixtures using `cat` do not model the production receiver's echo behavior. Any fixture-calibrated threshold is suspect; validate against the real Ink TUI.
- Argv-shape tests with scripted capturePaneFn stubs cannot catch this class of defect: they return exactly what the code expects. Real-tmux probes found every one of the regressions above.

PRIOR ART. The parked branch cam/issue-358 (origin, 64e2a909) holds the abandoned wrap/anchor attempt and is worth reading for what fails and why; do not resume it. The reviewer's real-tmux probes are described in the CAM-358 round-1 and round-2 review findings.

NOTE ON PRIORITY. This is latent, not the live operator bug: the reported lost pushes were 79-93 chars into a 138-column pane, so nothing wrapped. It becomes live on a narrower pane or a longer verdict line.

spec.scope: Replace the content-matching submission oracle in src/tmux/dispatch.ts with a pane-geometry oracle, and close the silent-loss gap at the call sites that pass no logEvent. isComposerEmptied(content, text) is retired in favour of a geometry probe that samples the tmux cursor position on the target pane (tmux display-message -p with a '#{cursor_x};#{cursor_y}' format) immediately BEFORE the send-keys and again after the existing SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS window; the composer counts as emptied only when the post-send cursor returns to the pre-send baseline. Add a shared display-message format-query helper under src/tmux/ (net-new: the only existing builder lives in the vendored src/retry/tmux.ts, uses an async Bun.spawn convention with no '-L cam' socket handling, and is not reachable from the dispatch path). Thread logEvent into the four sendKeysWhenIdle call sites that currently omit it so retry exhaustion always emits push-undelivered. Cover the behaviour with a real-tmux integration test at a pinned narrow pane width driving a WRAPPING payload end to end.
acceptanceCriteria: A payload longer than the pane width left un-submitted in the composer is reported NOT delivered and is retried: a real-tmux integration test at a pinned pane width (new-session -x 80) with a payload exceeding the composer's usable columns asserts send-keys is attempted maxAttempts times and exactly one push-undelivered event is emitted.
A payload that IS successfully submitted produces exactly ONE send-keys call and ZERO push-undelivered events, asserted in that same real-tmux test.

The oracle derives its verdict solely from tmux cursor geometry sampled from the target pane and never substring-matches the payload against captured pane content: grep -n 'includes(text)' src/tmux/dispatch.ts returns no results.
The empty-composer baseline is sampled per-send from the same pane immediately before send-keys; no absolute cursor coordinate is hardcoded anywhere in src/.

All four sendKeysWhenIdle call sites (src/commands/issue.ts, src/commands/review.ts, src/commands/spec.ts, src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts) pass a logEvent, so retry exhaustion emits push-undelivered on every production path rather than nothing.
bun run typecheck, bun test, and bun run check:all are all green.
gotchas: SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS stays load-bearing; do not remove it. Live probe against the real Ink TUI: after a genuine submit the cursor already reads the empty baseline at t+0, which is ALSO what an un-rendered pane reads before typed text appears. Geometry does not remove the settle requirement, so keep the existing settle window before the post-send sample.

cursor_y alone is useless as a signal. The Ink composer grows UPWARD from the bottom of the pane, so a three-row wrapped composer's last row has the SAME cursor_y as an empty composer. Measured on a real claude TUI: empty composer (2,26), wrapped composer (10,26), short filled composer (33,26). cursor_x carries the discriminating signal; compare the full (x,y) pair against the baseline and never key on y alone.

Never hardcode an absolute cursor coordinate. Opening a dialog relocates the cursor entirely: measured /help moving it to (9,6) in the same pane whose empty-composer baseline is (2,26). Only a per-send baseline comparison is sound.

Exact-wrap-boundary collision: when the payload length lands exactly on a wrap boundary the cursor can rest at the continuation row's start column, which may equal the empty-composer baseline x. The real-tmux test MUST include a payload sized to the wrap boundary for the pinned pane width, not merely an arbitrarily long one.

The live defect being fixed: isComposerEmptied currently evaluates lines.slice(-5).some(l => l.includes(text)). A wrapped payload never appears whole on any single line, so the predicate ALWAYS reports delivered, breaks the retry loop on attempt 1, and emits no event. Confirmed against a real Ink TUI capture, not inferred.

Three different capture readers are wired in production simultaneously: src/supervisor/host.ts:579 (full scrollback, capture-pane -p -S -) feeds the supervisor path, src/supervisor/host.ts:270 makeCapturePaneFn (visible screen) feeds all three src/commands/sidecar.ts notify sites, and src/tmux/dispatch.ts:221 (visible screen) is the default. A geometry oracle must produce the same verdict regardless of which reader is wired.
sendKeysVerified returns void and no caller can observe delivery. Do NOT change its signature in this issue; logEvent is the observability channel.

Reuse the established real-tmux harness pattern from test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts: a dedicated TEST_SOCK for socket isolation, the swapSocketSpawn SpawnFn that rewrites '-L cam' to the test socket so no live cam run session is touched, waitForCondition polling rather than fixed sleeps, and kill-server in beforeEach/afterEach. Gate the tests with test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable).
Do NOT resume, branch from, or cherry-pick the parked branch cam/abandoned/issue-358-oracle-attempt. It holds the abandoned content-matching attempt and is reference material only.
When building a multi-field tmux display-message format, use ';' as the field separator: tmux mangles a literal TAB to '_' in format output.

Argv-shape tests with scripted capturePaneFn stubs structurally CANNOT catch this class of defect, since they return exactly the string the code expects. The existing unit tests in test/dispatch.test.ts are all of that shape; the new coverage must drive a real tmux server.
